newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: New Zealander emerges as Burns Philp buyer.
newsitem.headline: New Zealander emerges as Burns Philp buyer.

text.p: New Zealand entrepreneur Graeme Hart emerged on Monday as the mystery buyer of a 16.24 percent stake in ailing food group Burns, Philp & Co Ltd, but analysts were uncertain about the strategy behind the purchase.
Hart had either built a strategic stake ahead of a possible third party takeover bid for the group, or believed he could add value, analysts contacted by Reuters said.
Most said the New Zealander, who spent A$2.50 a share for the bulk of his 86.14 million share stake, also appeared to have paid over the odds.
Burns Philp closed at A$2.03 last Thursday before news of the share raid and has traded in the A$2.00 to A$2.20 range in recent months.
"If he'd just sat in the market he could have picked it up for 25 cents a share less," said one analyst.
Hart, who last year sold his Whitcoulls printing, book retailing and stationary group for NZ$320 million, met Burns Philp management in Sydney before announcing his stake.
His private company Rank Group Ltd said in a statement that it intended to be a long-term shareholder.
The discussions were amicable and constructive and Rank "identified" with Burns Philp's current objectives, it added.
Sources at Burns Philp said this indicated broad support for plans to sell off the company's herb and spice business, and for its on-going search for a chief executive to replace Ian Clack
Burns Philp announced its exit from herbs and spices last month after a strategy to become a major international player failed to generate sufficient returns.
Clack announced his intention to step down at the same time.
A Burns Philp spokesman said board representation was also briefly discussed, but it was agreed it was not an immediate priority for either Hart or Burns Philp.
Further discussions would be held but no date was set.
Burns Philp has been seen as a potential takeover target following its recent woes, with fellow Australian food group Goodman Fielder Ltd keen to acquire its well performed yeast business.
However, the group's future is clouded by continuing legal action over the A$600 million collapse of Estate Mortgage Trusts in 1990. A group subsidiary was the Estate Mortgage trustee.
Analysts said Hart may have taken a view about the litigation in his decision to build up a strategic stake.
But he appeared to have little to offer Burns Philp, unlike other food companies, such as Goodman Fielder, which may have been able to extract savings through synergies with Burns Philp.
"I think it's very much an opportunistic move," said a Sydney-based analyst.
"But he's got to wait for someone to come in, which is a very big gamble," he said.
Another noted relations between Hart and Sir Ron Brierley, whose Australian vehicle Tyndall Australia Ltd is involved in the Estate Mortgage litigation, had been frosty in the past.
Rank said it holds a 14.9 percent shareholding in Burns Philp and, subject to Foreign Investment Review Board approval, is entitled to a further 1.3 percent under an option agreement.
Burns Philp closed down 3.8 cents at A$2.392 on Monday, a level that values Hart's parcel at A$206 million.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
